name noun and verb

also what’s your name?, my name is, be called, call, by name, by the name of

classical

Plaut. Amph. 364: quid nōmen tibi est?
Gell. 2.29.3: nōmen est cassīta
Traupman 15, 17: Quid est nōmen tibi?
Traupman 20

nōmen, nōminis n.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

“My name is Mark” is mihi nōmen est Mārcus, or Mārcō, the name in the dative beside mihi: cui Serviō Tulliō fuit nōmen (Liv. 1.39.1).

Other words

  • vocō, vocāre, vocāvī, vocātum — call (by a name), name

    verb, first conjugation · classical · Plaut. Amph. 365: Sōsiam vocant Thēbānī; M-O s.v. name: quī vocāris?; Traupman 286 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Quī vocāris?, what are you called?; vocor, my name is.

  • appellō, appellāre, appellāvī, appellātum — call, name; address by name

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 22.30.2: cum patrem Fabium appellāsset; Caes. BG 1.1: quī ipsōrum linguā Celtae, nostrā Gallī appellantur; Traupman 286 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    With two accusatives, as in Livy.

  • nōminō, nōmināre, nōmināvī, nōminātum — name; mention by name

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 26: amor enim, ex quō amīcitia nōmināta est; Traupman 103: eum nōlō nōmināre; Traupman 286 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • nōmen indere — give a name (to)

    also used · classical · Plaut. Men. 263: huic urbī nōmen Epidamnō inditumst; Liv. 1.34 (Lewis & Short)

    With a dative of the one named; not nōmen dare (below).

  • nuncupō, nuncupāre, nuncupāvī, nuncupātum — call by name, name

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short: “mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.; esp. in jurid. lang.”; Traupman 286 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • nōmen dare — enlist, give in one’s name

    avoid · classical · Liv. 2.24.2: nē nōmina darent

    A false friend: classically to enrol, above all for military service (Lewis & Short), not to name a child or a pet.

Examples

  • Quid ais? quid nōmen tibi est? — Sōsiam vocant Thēbānī, Dāvō prōgnātum patre.

    What’s that? What’s your name? — The Thebans call me Sosia, son of Davus.Plaut. Amph. 364–365

  • avicula … est parva, nōmen est cassīta

    There is a little bird; its name is cassita, the crested lark.Gell. 2.29.3

  • Periī hercle: nōmen perdidī.

    Oh no, I’ve forgotten the name.Ter. Ph. 386

  • lūdat lascīva … et nōmen blaesō garriat ōre meum

    let her play, full of fun, … and prattle my name with her lisping mouthMart. 5.34.7–8

  • nōmine Varrō

    Varro by nameTraupman 349

See also name day, word, language.
